why: This sits in the Trees week as an indexed tree problem. Insert positions into a Fenwick tree in decreasing value order, so when you handle nums[i] the tree holds exactly the positions of strictly greater values. The answer is the k-th marked position after i, which an order-statistic descent on the tree finds.
hints: If only the elements greater than nums[i] were 'switched on', you would need the k-th switched-on index to the right of i.
Sort indices by value descending and handle equal values as a group: query all of them first, then insert them, so 'strictly greater' holds.
Fenwick tree over positions: c = prefix(i). If total - c >= k, find the smallest p with prefix(p) >= c + k using binary lifting. Each step is O(log n), O(n log n) overall.
pitfalls: Equal values are not 'greater'. Insert a group of equal values only after querying it.
The output is 1-indexed positions, with -1 when fewer than k exist.
A per-index scan to the right is O(n^2), too slow at 1e5.
